name: Ho Chi Minh
role: Founder of the Indochinese Communist Party and president of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam (1945–1969)
summary: A Vietnamese Marxist-Leninist who moved from anti-colonial petitions in Paris to founding the Communist party and leading the Viet Minh and the DRV. He held that national liberation and communism went together, favoured a disciplined vanguard party, land redistribution and armed revolution, and ran a one-party state that also pursued reunification of Vietnam. He criticised personality cults and lived modestly.

public-ownership.rationale: His 1930 programme called for confiscating imperialist banks and enterprises and placing them under a worker-peasant-soldier government; he praised the Soviet model.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He described the DRV 1951-52 agricultural tax as graduated, exempting the poorest households and charging more as harvests grew.

unions-good.rationale: Wrote approvingly of workers organising in unions and striking, treated organisation and discipline as necessary, and the DRV had a General Confederation of Labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: Programme called for confiscating plantations and enterprises and distributing land to poor peasants; his government carried out land reform.

central-planning.rationale: Praised the Soviet Sixth Five-Year Plan as a brilliant success and set the goal of advancing to socialism in North Vietnam.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wanted land distributed to poor peasants, but also stressed public control of banks and industry, so the evidence is mixed.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Listed founding the National Bank of Vietnam and centralised state supervision of finance among the DRV's achievements.

one-party-rule.rationale: Described the Party as the leader of the people and the leading nucleus of the state, with Marxism-Leninism as its unshakable basis, while keeping a nominal united front.

land-redistribution.rationale: Programme in 1930 confiscated plantations of imperialists and reactionaries and gave them to poor peasants; he later led a government that carried out land reform.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Celebrated the overthrow of the monarchy that had ruled for dozens of centuries and its replacement by a republic; 1930 programme sought to overthrow Vietnamese feudalism.

democracy-best.rationale: Named his state a democratic republic and demanded elected representation, but advocated Party leadership and later ran a one-party state; mixed.

political-violence-never.rationale: Called revolution the only road to survival and urged everyone to fight the French with whatever weapons they had.

revolution-justified.rationale: Wrote that revolution was the only road to survival for the Vietnamese and led armed revolution and war.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Sought a worker-peasant-soldier government that would confiscate the property of imperialists and the reactionary bourgeoisie.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Stated that imperialist contradictions caused the 1914-18 war and that a second world war would follow from imperialist rivalries.

taxation-theft.rationale: Introduced and defended a state agricultural tax and counted tax reform among the DRV's achievements.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described colonial states and bourgeoisies as using the state machinery to oppress and indoctrinate the colonised and workers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Founded the Indochinese Communist Party as the party of the working class to lead the revolution and stressed iron discipline.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Told commanders that once a decision is taken it may not be discussed, only carried out; cited Lenin on near-military inner-party discipline.

party-commands-army.rationale: Credited the Central Committee with leading the campaign and described commissars working with commanders.

workers-own-party.rationale: Founded a communist party of the working class and urged communist parties to organise colonial workers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Appealed in 1919 and 1945 to the right of nations to self-determination.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Denounced colonial economies run for French capital, including forced crops, land seizures and taxes, and declared an end to colonial relations.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mocked the French "civilizing mission" as plunder and cruelty and declared the Vietnamese right to independence.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Condemned the racial hierarchy of pay, status and legal treatment in the colonies and demanded the same legal guarantees for Vietnamese as for Europeans.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Opened the Declaration by quoting that all peoples are equal from birth with rights to life, happiness and freedom; denounced unequal treatment of natives.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: In 1919 demanded that a system of laws replace the system of governing by decree.

bound-labor.rationale: Denounced forced labour and the reduction of peasants to serfs on land taken by planters, and sought land for the peasants.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Ended the monarchy and wrote that socialism cannot tolerate a personality cult, which existed to some degree in Vietnam.

leader-cult.rationale: In 1956 criticised the personality cult, admitting it existed in Vietnam and limited initiative; his Testament asked for a modest funeral.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Presented the end of monarchy and feudalism as a goal and achievement of the revolution.

elective-rulers.rationale: Welcomed replacing the monarchy with a democratic republic.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Claimed his government spoke for the whole people and called rivals puppets, but he also ran a party-led state.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Built a party and a united front as the organised channel between leader and people rather than bypassing them.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Announced the Thai-Meo Autonomous Region so minorities could run their own activities, as an integral part of Vietnam.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Condemned the French split of Vietnam into three regimes to wreck national unity and fought for a unified Vietnam.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Insisted on a unified Vietnam from 1946 to the Testament, which says north and south will certainly be reunited.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Accused the French of dividing Vietnam to wreck unity and said the US and southern authorities sought to perpetuate the partition.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Repealed all international obligations France had undertaken on Vietnam’s behalf and abolished French special rights.

rule-by-example.rationale: Stressed the moral example of cadres, but also strict discipline and the coercive land reform campaign.

people-in-arms.rationale: Called on all citizens to fight with any weapon and built militias, but also created a regular People’s Army.

state-harmful.rationale: Built a state and a government and spoke of the people as masters of a democratic state.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His government ran mass literacy and education, taxation and finance.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Reports say communist subordinates jailed non-communist nationalists and the party later ran a one-party state, but he promoted a broad united front.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Inferred: from his adoption of Marxism-Leninism as his doctrine and his call for class struggle.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: from his declared adoption of Marxism-Leninism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Urged workers to class struggle, though his united front also gathered classes against colonialism.

workers-nation.rationale: Insisted that genuine patriotism cannot be separated from proletarian internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Programme in 1930 called for equality between man and woman.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Attributed colonised peoples’ condition to imposed ignorance and an artificial racial hierarchy.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Argued Lenin refused to divide white and coloured peoples and urged workers of all races and colonial and metropolitan peoples to unite.

racial-franchise.rationale: Demanded equal rights, and representation in the French parliament, for Vietnamese.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Presented Vietnam as one family of Kinh, Tay, Nung, Thai, Meo and other nationalities with equality among them.

religious-nation.rationale: Front congress represented all religious beliefs and nationalities as one family.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Testament calls for complete selflessness, frugality and dedication to the public interest.

person-over-state.rationale: Told artists and soldiers to put the interests of the Resistance, the fatherland and the people above all.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Told the elderly that patriots never live idly and should keep taking part in national work.

gradual-change.rationale: Led revolution and war to change society rather than waiting for institutions to evolve.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Called Marxism-Leninism the unshakable basis and its purity to be defended.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Told cadres to respect people’s faith and customs, while also working gradually to reduce superstition.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Said the colonialist bourgeoisie crammed the home population with speeches, films, newspapers and exhibitions to build a colonial outlook.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Described the ruling class using both intense propaganda and fierce repression.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Documented how nine imperial countries drew profit and land from their colonies.

party-own-road.rationale: Said national features and conditions are an increasingly important factor in each party’s policy, while also stressing ideological unity.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Sought recognition and aid from the Soviet Union and China and said socialist solidarity was as necessary as in the resistance war.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Called the Soviet Union a triumph of socialism and fascists enemies, so would not equate them.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Called the Soviet Union the vanguard of the revolutionary camp and spoke of its great triumph of socialism.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Wrote that only socialism and communism can liberate oppressed nations, and paired independence with confiscation in his programme.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Confiscation programme targeted imperialist firms, and he condemned US companies monopolising Vietnam’s resources.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Condemned colonists and companies seizing land and called for confiscating imperialist plantations.

national-resource-control.rationale: Charged France with robbing Vietnam of mines, forests and raw materials and later denounced US firms’ control of natural resources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: From 1959 pressed the Politburo to send aid to the Viet Cong insurgency in South Vietnam.

non-intervention.rationale: Condemned French and US intervention in Vietnam but also pushed to aid the insurgency in the south.

defeat-communism.rationale: Held that only socialism and communism can liberate the oppressed and fought for communism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Regarded Leninism and communism as the path to socialism and rejected capitalism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Built and led armies and called for armed resistance.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Identified with the socialist camp and the camp of peace and democracy, and opposed SEATO and NATO.

close-ties-china.rationale: Welcomed People’s China’s recognition and example and spoke of the friendship of the two peoples.

dominated-front.rationale: Described the oppressed colonial peoples and the Soviet Union as one revolutionary camp against imperialism and urged the Vietnamese-Cambodian-Laotian bloc.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Demanded the withdrawal of foreign troops from Vietnam, though his state relied on Chinese and Soviet help.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Described his wars as defensive resistance, but his government also backed an insurgency in the south.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Said attempts to blemish the Soviet Union would fail and urged strengthening the socialist camp against imperialist plots.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Addressed his compatriots as martyrs and praised heroism and sacrifice in the Resistance.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Invoked historic national heroes such as Ly Thuong Kiet as models for today’s patriots.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Said patriotism led him to communism and that genuine patriotism cannot be separated from proletarian internationalism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Accused colonial capitalism of criminal exploitation, including starvation wages in new factories.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Exempted the poorest households from tax and sought land for poor peasants.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Attributed Vietnamese misery to colonial land seizure, taxes and exploitation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Said that in social life there are many professions and a division of work is inevitable.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: wrote sympathetically about strikes and criticised a government that refused to recognise a workers’ federation.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Defended a graduated agricultural tax with exemptions for the poorest.

moral-incentives.rationale: Promoted patriotic emulation and honours, and the Testament asks for selflessness, but also material provision for people.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: from his charge that owners exploit workers and his programme to take property for those who work it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: 1930 programme aimed at a worker-peasant-soldier government.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Gave a minority region its own autonomy over its economic and cultural life, within the state and under Party leadership.

notes: Most evidence comes from his own writings on the Marxists Internet Archive, which hold few statements on social, religious or technology topics. Some answers rest on later biographical reference material. The 1969 Testament was read in a Portuguese edition; wording was paraphrased. Land reform executions occurred under his government, which later apologised for errors in 1956; his own role in specifics is uncertain.
